A specifier that resolves for BOTH judges cannot exist in this lane (10-modules.errors.rip states why)

13-components.errors.rip.why: the ref-cell mismatch (an HTMLInputElement cell on a div) — the __ripRefCell admission rejects the cell argument (TS2345, anchored through the pair's cover); rip-native: React's ref rejection fires for a different reason (a raw element is not a Ref shape), so the twin cannot honestly judge it; pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)

the two-way bind mismatch (number state into a string prop) — no TSX line can spell the <=> channel; the container-typed message is the channel's real contract; pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)

a boolean attribute admits `boolean | null | undefined`, not any truthy value — the road states that type on the author's OWN expression, so an uncoerced string rejects where `!!` would have taken it; rip-native: a JSX attribute is an assignment (TS2322) and cannot spell a type stated on the expression, so the twin coerces (`!!label`) and stays quiet; pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)

25-components.errors.rip.why: the non-nullable ref cell's own initializer — the declaration is deliberately un-nullable so the ref row below can reject, and `:=` takes an initializer, so the same deliberate wrongness reports twice: once here and once at the ref; the TSX twin spells the cell nullable (useRef<T | null>) and carries neither

a tag-typed cell on a foreign tag — the same rip-native __ripRefCell admission as the row above, one tag apart (TS2345 on the cell argument); pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)

a forwarded element ref whose cell types a different tag than the child's own ref — no TSX line can spell the <=> channel, and the container-typed message is the channel's real contract; pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)

an array-typed reactive member whose initializer carries a wrong element — the mismatch rip publishes is between CELLS (the declared `{value: string[]}` against the inferred `{value: (string | number)[]}`), so it anchors on the member rather than on the element the twin flags; the twin's own array is correct and stays quiet
